title: Fighters Without Borders: Mercenaries, Adventurers, and Volunteers in Myanmar’s Civil War
gist: Russia–Myanmar military ties are deepening, with VDV troops training with the Myanmar military in the Tiger-2026 exercise and Min Aung Hlaing signing military and economic agreements in Moscow; beyond official cooperation, evidence suggests Russian 'soldiers of fortune' may already be fighting alongside Myanmar forces.

insights.claim: In July 2026 Russian Airborne Forces (VDV) trained alongside Myanmar troops in the Tiger-2026 joint exercise, part of expanding military cooperation between Naypyidaw and Moscow.
insights.speaker: Thurein Naing
insights.so_what: Russia is consolidating a Southeast Asian client; sanctions and arms-embargo dynamics around Myanmar are shifting.

insights.claim: After the exercise, Min Aung Hlaing visited Russia and signed agreements and memoranda on military and broader economic cooperation, calling Myanmar a 'reliable partner' of Russia.
insights.speaker: Thurein Naing
insights.so_what: Russian economic deals could give Moscow access to Myanmar resources and projects, competing with Chinese influence.
insights.locator: The exercise was followed by a visit

insights.claim: The Kremlin has become an important partner for Min Aung Hlaing's 'civilian' government, despite his earlier overtures appearing to get limited attention.
insights.speaker: Thurein Naing
insights.so_what: The regime's external backing looks more durable, lowering odds of near-term regime collapse.

insights.claim: The presence of VDV personnel, unmanned vehicles, and Russian military instructors in Myanmar has prompted observers to ask whether Moscow may become more deeply involved in the civil war.
insights.speaker: Thurein Naing
insights.so_what: Deeper Russian involvement would prolong Myanmar's conflict and raise risk for foreign projects in the country.
insights.locator: The presence in Myanmar of VDV

insights.claim: Recent evidence suggests Russian 'soldiers of fortune' may already be operating alongside Myanmar forces, raising the possibility of a more direct Russian presence on the battlefield beyond official cooperation.
insights.speaker: Thurein Naing
insights.so_what: Unofficial Russian combatants mirror patterns seen in Africa; watch for escalation and Western sanctions responses.
insights.locator: But Moscow’s growing official military presence
